subject: R Session Aborted with Detection Covariates

messages.author: e54c74980a01d9ed
messages.subject: R Session Aborted with Detection Covariates
parts:
Hi everyone,

When I add the covariate of wind speed or dew point to my detection model, the R session is immediately aborted with a message saying "R encountered a fatal error. The session was terminated." And I have to start a new session. Has anyone else had this problem/have any advice? Here is my code:

data <- read.csv("2021_WinterSeason.csv")

#all continuous variables are standardized here to have a zero mean and unit variance
date <-as.matrix(data[ , 6:9])
sd.date <- sd(c(date), na.rm = TRUE)
mean.date <- mean(date, na.rm = TRUE)
date <- (date - mean.date)/sd.date

temp <-as.matrix(data[ , 10:13])
sd.temp <- sd(c(temp), na.rm = TRUE)
mean.temp <- mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE)
temp <- (temp - mean.temp)/sd.temp

wind <-as.matrix(data[ , 14:17])
sd.wind  <- sd(c(wind ), na.rm = TRUE)
mean.wind  <- mean(wind , na.rm = TRUE)
wind  <- (wind  - mean.wind )/sd.wind 

dewpt <-as.matrix(data[ , 18:21])
sd.dewpt  <- sd(c(dewpt ), na.rm = TRUE)
mean.dewpt  <- mean(dewpt , na.rm = TRUE)
dewpt  <- (dewpt  - mean.dewpt )/sd.dewpt 

#Visualize data to see if normally distributed
hist(date)
hist(temp)
hist(wind)
hist(dewpt)

y <- data[ ,2:5] #these are the camera events weeks 1-4

siteCovs <- data[ ,10:21] #land cover

obsCovs <- list(date = data[ ,6:9])

umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, siteCovs = siteCovs, obsCovs = list(date = date))
summary(umf)

# A model with constant parameters- NULL model
(fm0 <- occu(~1 ~1, umf))
confint(fm0, type = "det", level = .85) #confidence intervals


#detection: date, occupancy: null
(fm1 <- occu(~date ~1, umf))
confint(fm1, type = "det", level = .85)

(fm2 <- occu(~wind ~1, umf))
confint(fm2, type = "det", level = 0.85)

#Detection: week, occupancy: null
(fm3 <- occu(~dewpt ~1, umf))
confint(fm3, type = "det", level = .85)


Thanks in advance!
Maria

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: R Session Aborted with Detection Covariates
parts:
It looks like you didn't put wind speed or dewpoint into your obsCovs when you made the umf. Can you try doing that?

Regardless you should not get an R crash as a result of a missing covariate. If you are able to email me your data CSV off-list I can try to find the problem.

Ken
